title: Savoy Newspaper Publisher Many Years Dies At 72
text:
MRS. J. B. MAY

Savoy Newspaper Publisher Many Years Dies At 72

SAVOY—Mrs. J. B. May, 72, former correspondent for the Sherman Democrat and publisher of the Savoy Star for 41 years, died at the family home at Savoy Saturday at 9:25 a. m. She was a native of Van Alstyne. She had been ill for two years.

Funeral arrangements are incomplete, but will probably be held Tuesday, pending the arrival of a sister, Mrs. M. Henry Gant of Miami, Fla.

The service is scheduled for the Savoy Church of Christ with Robert D. Bankes, Church of Christ minister of Sherman, conducting the service. Burial will be in Sunnyside Cemetery, Savoy, directed by Earnheart-Strickland Funeral Home.

Mrs. May was born May 4, 1878, a daughter of the late Mr. and Mrs. T. P. Buford. She was married to T. E. Arterberry. He died in 1925. On May 31, 1932, she was married to J. B. May. She attended Haskell College at Savoy and published the Savoy Star from April 1902 until June, 1943.

She had a dress, hat and gift shop at Savoy. At one time, Mrs. May taught in the Savoy schools. She was a past secretary of the Savoy College Ex-Students Association, and officer and leader in the Civil League and was a member of the Church of Christ.

Survivors include her husband, J. B. May of Savoy; one sister, Mrs. Gant; two nieces, Mrs. Roy Booth of Waco, Mrs. Cy Kaulback of San Antonio; a great-niece, Miss Martha Frances Booth of Waco, one nephew, Buford Penlace of Dallas; one step-daughter, Mrs. O. L. Jones of Whitewright and three grandchildren.
